main_text.head: Quid est Scheva?
main_text.p: Scheva est vocalis brevissima e, sub consona posita hoc modo, בְ. Et legitur aut quiescit.
main_text.head: Ubi legitur?
main_text.p: In principio vocis, ut, דְבִיר debir, ora-culum. Deinde in medio post vocales lon-gas, ut פָּקְדוּ pakedú. שֹׁמְרִים schomerim.
Tertiò, sub consona Dagessata, ⁊[?] sub consona cujus similis sequitur, ut דִּבְּרוּ dibberú, locuti sunt: הַלְלוּ halelú, lau-date.[?]
Quartò, in medio vocis, scheva geminato, prius quiescit, posterius legitur, ut יִפְקְדוּ jiphkedú.
main_text.head: Ubi quiescit?
main_text.p: Primò in medio vocis post vocales breves, ut פִּקְדוּ pikdú. nisi sequatur gut-turalis: ut, מַלְאָךְ maleách.
Secundò, in fine vocis non solû simplex, sed etiam geminum scheva quiescit, licèt

page.notes: The symbol after "Tertiò, sub consona Dagessata," is not clearly legible and is transcribed as ⁊[?]. The end of "lau-date" is a doubtful mark, shown as .[?]. Hebrew vowel points are transcribed from the scan and may differ in fine detail. The first-line sheva sign is a close reading. The paragraph ending "licèt" continues on the next page.
